ability_score_generator.automatic_trigger: After both an approved race/species and a starting class are selected.

5e.meaning_in_this_file: The original fifth-edition rules first published in 2014.

5_5e.meaning_in_this_file: The updated fifth-edition rules first published in the 2024 core rulebooks.

compatibility_summary: Both are versions of fifth edition rather than unrelated game systems.
Adventures and much supporting content can be used across versions, but player-facing rules elements with the same name should normally use one chosen version rather than being combined line by line.
A campaign should declare a baseline ruleset and clearly label any imported legacy or updated options.
edition_identity.table_rule: When a 5e and 5.5e rule conflict, use the version chosen by the DM for that campaign or character option; do not silently blend contradictory procedures.

five_minute_explanation: One player is the Dungeon Master (DM). The DM describes the world, portrays nonplayer characters and monsters, and decides when the rules or dice are needed.
Each other player controls one adventurer and says what that character tries to do.
The usual rhythm is: the DM describes a situation; players describe actions; the DM resolves the result through narration, a rule, or a die roll.
Most uncertain actions use a twenty-sided die: roll 1d20, add the relevant modifier, and compare the total with a target number.
The goal is collaborative play and an interesting shared story, not defeating the DM or mechanically winning every scene.
minimum_materials: A character sheet for each player character
A set of polyhedral dice or a digital roller
The rules for the chosen edition
An adventure, scenario, or situation for the DM to run
A shared understanding of tone, boundaries, schedule, and table expectations

first_session_recommendation.session_length: About 2–4 hours, depending on the group
first_session_recommendation.scope: One clear goal, one social or exploration obstacle, and one manageable combat or other high-stakes challenge
teaching_order: class features and spells as they arise

dungeon_master: Calls for rolls only when the outcome is both uncertain and meaningful.
Sets or applies target numbers, tracks consequences, and makes rulings when no rule directly answers the situation.
Protects spotlight balance, pacing, clarity, and table safety.
players: Decide what their characters attempt and how they approach it.
Know the main features, attacks, spells, and resources on their sheets.
Roll when the DM or a rule calls for a roll; do not pre-roll to force a result.
React to consequences and help build the fiction with the rest of the group.

core_loop.name: Describe
core_loop.procedure: The DM explains the current situation and what the characters can immediately perceive.

core_loop.name: Choose
core_loop.procedure: Players describe their characters’ intentions and actions in ordinary language.

core_loop.name: Resolve
core_loop.procedure: The DM narrates an automatic result or calls for a rule or D20 Test.

core_loop.name: Change the situation
core_loop.procedure: Apply success, failure, costs, discoveries, damage, conditions, or new choices.

core_loop.name: Repeat
core_loop.procedure: Continue until the scene, encounter, session, or adventure ends.

three_common_pillars.social_interaction: Conversations, negotiations, deception, intimidation, relationships, and reading motives.
three_common_pillars.exploration: Travel, investigation, navigation, hazards, secrets, puzzles, and interacting with environments.
three_common_pillars.combat: Structured rounds and turns when precise timing and hostile actions matter.

session_zero_and_table_practice.classification: Recommended table practice, not a single mandatory core rule.
decisions_to_make: Choose 5e or 5.5e as the rules baseline.
Agree on allowed books, third-party content, homebrew, and how legacy options will be imported.
Set campaign tone, expected themes, character cooperation, and player-versus-player boundaries.
Discuss content lines, veils, pause tools, accessibility needs, and how anyone can request a break.
Set scheduling, attendance, communication, dice visibility, leveling method, and replacement-character procedure.
good_table_norms: Ask before taking control of another player character’s choices.
Separate character conflict from player conflict.
Share spotlight and avoid interrupting another player’s key moment.
Correct rules briefly during play; move longer debates to a break or after the session unless the ruling is high impact.

dice_and_notation.notation: XdY + Z means roll X dice with Y sides, total them, then add Z. A minus sign subtracts instead.

dice.d4: Small damage, healing, and random tables
dice.d6: Common weapon and spell dice; also used for ability-score generation
dice.d8: Common martial, healing, and class Hit Die
dice.d10: Weapons, class Hit Dice, and percentile tens digit
dice.d12: Large weapon or class damage and Barbarian Hit Die
dice.d20: Ability checks, saving throws, attack rolls, initiative, and death saves
dice.d100: Percentile results, normally rolled with two d10s

reading_examples.meaning: Roll two d6, add both dice, then add 3.
Roll four d8 and total them.
Roll percentile dice for a result from 1 to 100; 00 and 0 normally represent 100.

identity_and_story: species or race depending on edition

core_numbers.ability_scores_and_modifiers: Six broad capabilities; most rolls use the modifier rather than the raw score.
core_numbers.proficiency_bonus: Added only when the character is proficient in the relevant skill, save, weapon, tool, or other listed use.
core_numbers.armor_class: The attack-roll target number needed to hit the character.
core_numbers.hit_points: Current durability; track current HP, maximum HP, temporary HP, and Hit Point/Hit Dice resources.
core_numbers.speed: How far the character can normally move on a turn.
core_numbers.initiative: Usually a Dexterity-based roll that determines turn order.
core_numbers.passive_perception: A standing awareness value, commonly 10 plus relevant modifiers.

offense: mastery property if using 5.5e and unlocked
character_sheet_tour.beginner_tip: Before play, mark your usual attack bonus, damage, AC, save DC, and the action type of each frequently used feature.

shared_principles: Start with a concept that can cooperate with the campaign’s premise and the other player characters.
Choose a class whose normal turn and resource complexity fit the player’s interests.
Record every proficiency, feature, language, item, spell, and numerical calculation instead of relying on memory.
Ask the DM which edition, books, optional rules, and ability-score method are in use before finalizing the character.
5e_2014_sequence: Determine ability scores, then apply racial increases from the selected option.
Describe the character, including background and personal characteristics.
Bring the party together and establish relationships or reasons to adventure.
5_5e_sequence: Determine origin by choosing a background, species, and languages.
Determine ability scores and apply the increases supplied by the background.
Choose alignment and other descriptive details if the table uses them.
Choose equipment from class and background options or permitted starting funds.
Calculate modifiers, AC, HP, attacks, saving throws, skills, and spell values.

ability_score_methods.point_buy: A controlled allocation method; use the edition’s published costs and DM approval.
ability_score_methods.rolled: A common method is 4d6, drop the lowest die, repeated six times; use only if the DM chooses this method.

background_difference.5e: Primarily grants skills, tools/languages, equipment, a feature, and story prompts; ability increases normally come from race in the 2014 core rules.
background_difference.5_5e: Carries ability-score increases, an Origin feat, two skill proficiencies, a tool proficiency, and equipment or funds.

species_race_difference.5e: The core rules use the term race and attach ability-score increases and other traits to that choice.
species_race_difference.5_5e: The core rules use species; species supplies creature traits, size/speed, and special traits, while background supplies ability-score increases.

class_selection_questions: Do you want most turns to focus on weapons, spells, support, stealth, transformation, or a mix?
Do you enjoy managing a long spell list and several limited resources?
Would you rather specialize strongly or have many flexible tools?
Does the party already cover healing, scouting, front-line durability, social influence, or knowledge—and does that matter to your group?

d20_test_types.ability_check: Attempts to overcome a challenge through an ability, often with a skill or tool proficiency.
d20_test_types.saving_throw: Attempts to avoid or resist a threat when a rule calls for a save.
d20_test_types.attack_roll: Attempts to hit a target; the total is compared with Armor Class.

core_mechanics.general_formula: 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + proficiency bonus if applicable + other bonuses or penalties
core_mechanics.success_rule: A total that equals or exceeds the target number succeeds unless a specific rule says otherwise.

advantage_disadvantage.advantage: Roll two d20s and use the higher result.
advantage_disadvantage.disadvantage: Roll two d20s and use the lower result.
advantage_disadvantage.cancellation: If at least one source of each applies, roll normally; multiple sources normally do not stack into more dice.

proficiency.use: Add the proficiency bonus only when a rule says the character is proficient in the relevant thing.
proficiency.no_double_addition: Do not add the same proficiency bonus twice unless a feature explicitly changes it, such as Expertise doubling it.

common_formulas.weapon_attack: 1d20 + attack ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient
common_formulas.weapon_damage: weapon damage dice + the attack ability modifier unless the rule says otherwise
common_formulas.passive_check: 10 + all modifiers that normally apply to the check; advantage/disadvantage may alter passive values under the applicable rules

when_not_to_roll: The task is automatic and no meaningful failure is possible.
The task is impossible in the established fiction.
Repeated rolling would merely delay an inevitable result with no changing stakes.
A rule directly resolves the outcome without a check.

procedure: State what your character wants from the other creature.
Choose an approach: honest persuasion, deception, intimidation, performance, empathy, bargaining, evidence, magic, or another tactic.
Roleplay as much or as little dialogue as the group enjoys; a player may summarize an approach instead of performing it.
The DM considers the creature’s goals, attitude, knowledge, leverage, and limits.
Roll only when the result is uncertain and the outcome matters.

common_checks.Intimidation: Threats, pressure, or force of presence
common_checks.Animal Handling: Influencing or understanding appropriate beasts or similar creatures

social_interaction.important_limit: A successful Charisma check is not mind control. It changes what is plausible within the target’s motives, attitude, and circumstances.
social_interaction.5_5e_note: The updated rules formalize Influence as an action and provide clearer attitude-based guidance; the DM still determines what is possible.

player_questions: Where are we going and what route are we taking?
Who is leading, scouting, watching, mapping, or searching?
What light sources, tools, spells, vehicles, or supplies are active?
What exactly are we examining or interacting with?
How much time are we willing to spend and what risks are we accepting?

common_checks.Investigation: Reason from clues or search methodically for how something works.
common_checks.Survival: Track, navigate, forage, or handle natural hazards.
common_checks.Athletics: Climb, jump, swim, break, or endure physical force where a check is needed.
common_checks.Acrobatics: Balance, tumble, or perform agile movement.
common_checks.Arcana_History_Nature_Religion: Recall specialized lore or study evidence related to those fields.

time_and_consequences: Searching carefully can consume time, change encounter risk, or use supplies.
Failed checks should often reveal a consequence, cost, incomplete result, or changed situation rather than simply stopping play.
Passive scores can help the DM resolve ongoing awareness without repeated rolls.

5_5e: determine whether anyone is caught unawares
roll initiative with surprise effects applied

round_and_turn.round_duration: About 6 seconds in the game world.
normal_turn_budget: one Bonus Action only if a rule grants one
one Reaction between the starts of your turns if triggered and available
round_and_turn.flexibility: Movement can usually be split before, between, and after actions or attacks, subject to the applicable rules.

main_actions.Attack: Make weapon attacks or Unarmed Strikes as allowed by the action and Extra Attack.
main_actions.Dash: Gain additional movement for the turn.
main_actions.Disengage: Avoid provoking Opportunity Attacks from movement for the rest of the turn.
main_actions.Dodge: Defend until the start of the next turn; exact benefits depend on the edition wording.
main_actions.Help: Assist an ally’s check or attack, or administer first aid under the applicable rule.
main_actions.Hide: Attempt to conceal yourself; the procedure differs between editions.
main_actions.Ready: Define a perceivable trigger and prepare an action or movement using your Reaction.
main_actions.Search: Actively look for hidden or non-obvious information.
main_actions.Use_or_Utilize: Interact with an object when the interaction requires an action.
main_actions.Magic_5_5e: Cast an action-time spell or activate an effect that specifically uses the Magic action.
main_actions.Influence_Study_5_5e: Updated named actions for changing attitudes or making structured knowledge checks.

attack_sequence: Choose a legal target and attack method.
Determine range, visibility, cover, advantage, disadvantage, and other modifiers.
Roll the attack: 1d20 plus the attack bonus.
Compare the total with the target’s AC.
On a hit, roll and apply damage and any additional effect.
combat.critical_hits: A natural 20 on an attack roll is a critical hit under the normal rules; roll the attack’s damage dice twice and add modifiers once, subject to feature-specific wording.
combat.opportunity_attacks: Normally use a Reaction to make one melee attack immediately before a visible creature leaves your reach through qualifying movement. Forced movement and teleportation generally do not provoke unless a rule says otherwise.

cover.total: cannot be targeted directly by effects that require a clear target through the cover

surprise_comparison.5e: A surprised creature cannot move or take an action on its first turn and cannot take a Reaction until that turn ends.
surprise_comparison.5_5e: A surprised creature has Disadvantage on its Initiative roll; it otherwise takes its turn normally.

grapple_and_shove_comparison.5e: Grapple and shove are special melee attacks using a Strength (Athletics) contest against the target’s Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics).
grapple_and_shove_comparison.5_5e: An Unarmed Strike can deal damage, grapple, or shove. Grapple and shove normally force a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against a DC based on the attacker’s Strength and proficiency.

weapon_mastery_5_5e.rule: A weapon’s mastery property is usable only by a character feature that unlocks mastery for that weapon.

properties.Cleave: Can enable a limited follow-up attack against a nearby second creature after a qualifying hit.
properties.Graze: Can deal limited ability-modifier damage on a miss.
properties.Nick: Moves the Light-property extra attack into the Attack action under its limits.
properties.Push: Can move a hit target away.
properties.Sap: Can hinder the target’s next attack.
properties.Slow: Can reduce the target’s Speed temporarily.
properties.Topple: Can force a save to knock the target Prone.
properties.Vex: Can set up Advantage on a later attack against the same target.

turn_checklist: Where do I need to move?
What action best advances the goal?
Do I have a useful Bonus Action?
Do I need to save my Reaction?

damage_healing_and_death.hit_points: Hit Points represent durability and the ability to keep fighting; losing HP normally has no mechanical effect until a creature reaches 0 unless another rule triggers.
damage_process: subtract remaining damage from current HP
temporary_hit_points: do not stack; choose the old or new amount
do not wake a creature at 0 HP
dropping_to_zero: check for instant death from massive remaining damage or another rule
make death saving throws at the start of turns while at 0 HP

death_saves.damage_at_zero: normally causes failures; a Critical Hit causes two

damage_healing_and_death.stabilizing: A successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check can normally stabilize a creature under the applicable Help/first-aid rule, and some items or magic do so automatically.

knocking_out.5e: When a melee attack reduces a creature to 0 HP, the attacker can declare the creature unconscious and stable instead of dead.
knocking_out.5_5e: A melee attack can instead reduce the target to 1 HP and make it Unconscious, beginning a Short Rest under the updated rule.

short_rest.shared_core: About 1 hour of light activity; characters can spend Hit Dice/Hit Point Dice to recover HP and may recharge features.
short_rest.5e: Spend Hit Dice at the end of the rest; a long rest restores half the character’s total Hit Dice, minimum one.
short_rest.5_5e: Spend Hit Point Dice on completion; the glossary explicitly lists interruptions such as initiative, non-cantrip spellcasting, or taking damage.

long_rest.shared_core: At least 8 hours, usually including at least 6 hours of sleep and no more than 2 hours of light activity; a creature must begin with at least 1 HP.
long_rest.5e: Regain all HP and up to half of total Hit Dice; normally no more than one benefit per 24 hours.
long_rest.5_5e: Regain all HP and all spent Hit Point Dice, restore reduced ability scores, reduce Exhaustion by 1, and wait at least 16 hours before starting another Long Rest. An interrupted rest can be resumed with added time under the glossary procedure.

levels.3: Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

5_5e.d20_tests: Subtract 2 times the Exhaustion level from every D20 Test.
5_5e.speed: Reduce Speed by 5 feet times the Exhaustion level.
5_5e.recovery: A Long Rest normally removes one level.

cantrips_and_leveled_spells.cantrip: Level 0 spell, normally cast without spending a spell slot.
cantrips_and_leveled_spells.leveled_spell: Level 1–9 spell; normally requires access, preparation or knowledge as appropriate, and a slot of the spell’s level or higher unless another rule says otherwise.

known_prepared_and_always_prepared: A class feature determines which spells are available and when the list can change.
An always-prepared spell does not normally count against a changeable prepared-spell limit unless a rule says otherwise.
Preparing a spell and having a spell slot are separate requirements: preparation grants access; the slot pays for most casts.
spell_slots: slots are expended to cast most leveled spells
using a higher-level slot may improve a spell only when its text says so
some features cast without slots or use separate Pact Magic rules

attack_and_save_spells.spell_attack: Caster rolls 1d20 + spellcasting modifier + proficiency against AC.
attack_and_save_spells.saving_throw_spell: Target rolls the specified save against the caster’s spell save DC.
attack_and_save_spells.automatic_effect: Some spells require neither an attack nor a save but may have other limits.

components.V: Verbal; speech or sound is required.
components.S: Somatic; prescribed movement is required, often needing a free hand under the applicable component rules.
components.M: Material; a component pouch, focus, or listed material is used. Costly or consumed materials follow the spell’s exact wording.

concentration.one_at_a_time: Starting another concentration effect ends the first.
concentration.damage_save: After damage, make a Constitution save; the normal DC is 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher. The updated glossary caps this DC at 30.

spellcasting.rituals: A ritual casting normally adds 10 minutes and avoids spending a slot, but only if the caster has a feature allowing that spell to be cast as a ritual and the spell has the Ritual tag.
spellcasting.casting_in_armor: A caster must have the relevant armor proficiency/training to cast while wearing that armor.

multiple_spells_on_a_turn.5e: Casting a spell as a Bonus Action prevents casting another spell that turn except a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action.
multiple_spells_on_a_turn.5_5e: A character can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell on a turn. Cantrips and slot-free casting can still interact with the action economy, triggers, and feature wording.

beginner_spell_turn: check line of sight/cover if relevant
spend the correct slot or resource
record duration and any ongoing condition

leveling_methods.experience_points: The DM awards XP; characters level when they reach the published threshold.
leveling_methods.milestone_or_story: The DM advances characters after significant goals, chapters, or accomplishments.

on_level_up: update proficiency bonus when the tier changes
update spells and slots as the class directs
apply feats or ability-score changes when granted
recalculate attacks, saves, skills, AC, DCs, and passive values
limited_resources: mark what recharges on a Short Rest
mark what recharges on a Long Rest
track uses separately from spell slots
do not assume similarly named resources are interchangeable
advancement_and_resources.multiclassing_warning: Multiclassing adds prerequisites and special rules for proficiencies, spell slots, and class features. New players should use it only after reading the chosen edition’s full multiclass rules.

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding proficiency to every d20 roll
common_mistakes.correction: Add it only when the character is proficient and the rule calls for it.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating a natural 20 as automatic success on every ability check
common_mistakes.correction: Automatic hit/critical rules apply to attack rolls; checks and saves follow their own rules unless the table uses a house rule.
Describe the action first so the DM can decide whether a roll is needed and which roll applies.
Advantage does not normally stack; one Advantage and one Disadvantage cancel.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using a Bonus Action automatically every turn
common_mistakes.correction: A Bonus Action exists only when a feature, spell, or rule grants one.
A creature normally concentrates on only one effect at a time.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using 5e surprise, grappling, exhaustion, or spell limits in a 5.5e game without noticing
common_mistakes.correction: These are among the most important edition-sensitive procedures; label the campaign baseline clearly.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming a successful social check forces any request
common_mistakes.correction: The DM determines what is plausible for the target; a check is not mind control.

common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting cover, range, visibility, or concentration
common_mistakes.correction: Check these before resolving attacks and spells.
Use the complete chosen version of a class, spell, feat, species/race, background, or rule element unless an official compatibility instruction says otherwise.

worked_examples.name: Ability check
worked_examples.situation: A proficient character with Strength 16 and proficiency bonus +2 tries to force open a stuck door.
worked_examples.calculation: Strength modifier +3; proficiency applies if the DM calls for Strength (Athletics), so roll 1d20 + 5 against the DC.
worked_examples.lesson: The DM chooses the ability and whether a skill proficiency applies based on the approach.

worked_examples.name: Weapon attack
worked_examples.situation: A character attacks with a proficient finesse weapon using Dexterity 16 and proficiency bonus +2.
worked_examples.calculation: Attack is 1d20 + 3 Dexterity + 2 proficiency = 1d20 + 5. On a hit, add the Dexterity modifier to the weapon’s damage unless a rule says otherwise.
worked_examples.lesson: Attack bonus and damage bonus are related but not identical calculations.

worked_examples.name: Saving throw spell
worked_examples.situation: A spellcaster with spellcasting ability 16 and proficiency bonus +2 casts a spell requiring a save.
worked_examples.calculation: Spell save DC = 8 + 3 + 2 = 13. The target rolls the specified saving throw against DC 13.
worked_examples.lesson: The caster normally does not roll an attack when the spell calls for a saving throw.

worked_examples.name: Concentration after damage
worked_examples.calculation: Half the damage is 9, so the normal concentration DC is 10, the higher value.
worked_examples.lesson: Concentration is a Constitution saving throw, not an ability check.

worked_examples.name: Edition-sensitive surprise
worked_examples.situation: The party ambushes an unaware guard.
worked_examples.calculation: In 5e, the surprised guard loses normal first-turn activity and reactions as defined. In 5.5e, the guard rolls Initiative with Disadvantage.
worked_examples.lesson: Confirm the campaign edition before applying surprise.

one or more obstacles with flexible solutions
stat blocks or DCs likely to matter
during_play: clarify intent before calling for a roll
use failure to change the situation
keep turn order visible in combat
ruling_method: choose the closest rule or an ability and proficiency
set a DC or opposed procedure
review after the session if the ruling will recur
dm_quickstart.encounter_advice: Do not rely only on raw damage. Mix terrain, objectives, movement, negotiation, hazards, time pressure, and retreat options.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Labeled 5e on D&D Beyond since March 2, 2026.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Labeled 5.5e on D&D Beyond since March 2, 2026.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Use these labels in filenames, character records, and menus to prevent accidental mixing.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Race, class, ability scores, description/background, equipment, party connection.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Class, origin (background/species/languages), ability scores, details, equipment, calculations.
edition_comparison.table_impact: The same concept can be rebuilt, but bonuses and feat sources move.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Normally supplied by race in the 2014 core rules.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Do not apply both systems to the same character without an explicit conversion rule.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Skills, tools/languages, equipment, background feature, and personality prompts.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Ability-score increases, Origin feat, skills, tool, and equipment/funds.
edition_comparison.table_impact: A legacy background requires the updated-book compatibility procedure when used with a 5.5e character.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Term is race; includes ability increases and traits.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Term is species; includes biological/magical traits, size, and Speed, while background carries ability increases.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Use the complete option from one rules version.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Feats are generally optional and commonly replace an Ability Score Improvement.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Feats are categorized as Origin, General, Fighting Style, and Epic Boon; backgrounds grant an Origin feat.
edition_comparison.table_impact: 5.5e characters normally begin with a feat through background.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Not a general core weapon system.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Weapons have mastery properties unlocked by specific class features.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Do not apply mastery effects unless the character has a feature that unlocks them.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Includes Cast a Spell and Use an Object among the familiar combat actions.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Uses Magic and Utilize and adds formal Influence and Study actions, among glossary revisions.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Features may refer to the new action names; read the exact version used.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Spend Inspiration to gain Advantage on an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Heroic Inspiration lets you reroll any die immediately after rolling and use the new result.
edition_comparison.table_impact: The resource has a materially different effect.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: A surprised creature cannot move or act on its first turn and cannot react until that turn ends.
edition_comparison.table_impact: This substantially changes ambush timing and should never be blended accidentally.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Special melee attacks resolved by Athletics contests.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Options of an Unarmed Strike, normally resolved by a Strength or Dexterity save against the attacker’s DC.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Builds and monster interactions can change because the resolution method changes.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Six-level table with different cumulative penalties at each level.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Each level gives -2 to D20 Tests and -5 feet Speed; death at level 6.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Restores all HP and up to half of total Hit Dice.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Restores all HP and all Hit Point Dice, restores reduced ability scores, and reduces Exhaustion by 1; interruption/resumption rules are more explicit.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Stealth is compared with passive Perception or active search under situational concealment rules.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: The Hide action specifies concealment prerequisites and a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check; the result becomes the search DC while hidden.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Use the complete edition procedure, including how the hidden state ends.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: A Bonus Action spell restricts other spellcasting that turn to a one-action cantrip.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: Only one spell slot can be expended to cast a spell on a turn.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Reaction, cantrip, Action Surge, and slot-free interactions must be checked against the chosen wording.

edition_comparison.5e_2014: Legacy class, spell, feat, item, or other option remains usable when the table permits it.
edition_comparison.5_5e_2024: The updated Player’s Handbook version replaces the 2014 version when using that book, with stated exceptions and compatibility guidance.
edition_comparison.table_impact: Choose one version of a same-named element rather than combining their best clauses.

importing_a_legacy_option_into_5_5e: Confirm the option is not already replaced by a 5.5e version with the same name.

For an older background, apply the current origin compatibility procedure rather than stacking old and new benefits.

quick_reference.d20_test: Roll 1d20 + ability modifier + proficiency if applicable + other modifiers; meet or exceed DC or AC.
quick_reference.attack: 1d20 + attack ability modifier + proficiency if proficient vs AC; on hit roll damage.
quick_reference.concentration_save: Constitution save DC 10 or half damage, whichever is higher; 5.5e glossary maximum DC 30.
quick_reference.death_save: d20: 10+ success; 9- failure; three successes stabilize; three failures die; natural 1 = two failures; natural 20 = 1 HP.

table_role_overview.dm: The Dungeon Master describes scenes, presents consequences, controls monsters/NPCs, and decides when a roll is needed.
table_role_overview.players: Players describe what their characters attempt, roll when the DM calls for uncertainty, and roleplay the results.
core_loop: Players describe what their characters do.
DM resolves the action through narration, rules, or dice.

dice_notation.format: XdY+Z means roll X dice with Y sides and add Z.

examples.meaning: Roll one twenty-sided die and add 4.
Roll two six-sided dice, add them together, then add 3.
In 5e, commonly simulated by rolling 1d6, dividing by 2, and rounding up.

d20_tests.definition: A D20 Test is a d20 roll used when the result is uncertain and meaningful. It covers ability checks, saving throws, and attack rolls.
d20_tests.formula: 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient + other bonuses/penalties
d20_tests.success_rule: If the total equals or exceeds the target number, the test succeeds.

advantage_and_disadvantage.advantage: Roll two d20s and use the higher result.
advantage_and_disadvantage.disadvantage: Roll two d20s and use the lower result.
advantage_and_disadvantage.both: If both apply, they cancel to a normal single d20 roll unless a feature says otherwise.

common_roll_formulas.ability_check: 1d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus if relevant
common_roll_formulas.skill_check: 1d20 + default or DM-chosen ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient in that skill
common_roll_formulas.expertise_check: 1d20 + ability modifier + double proficiency bonus if expertise applies
common_roll_formulas.saving_throw: 1d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient in that save
common_roll_formulas.weapon_attack: 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient with the weapon
common_roll_formulas.weapon_damage: weapon damage dice + relevant ability modifier unless a rule says otherwise
common_roll_formulas.passive_check: 10 + relevant modifiers that normally apply to the check
common_roll_formulas.death_saving_throw: 1d20 with no normal ability modifier; 10 or higher succeeds, 9 or lower fails; track 3 successes or 3 failures.

combat_basics.initiative: At combat start, each participant rolls initiative. Higher results act earlier.
turn_resources: one reaction between turns when triggered
free/object interactions as allowed by DM
attack_resolution: Roll attack if the action calls for one.
On a hit, roll damage and apply effects.

spellcasting_basics.cantrips: At-will spells that do not use spell slots.
spellcasting_basics.leveled_spells: Usually require spending a spell slot of the spell level or higher.
spellcasting_basics.spell_attack_vs_save: Some spells use a spell attack roll; some force the target to make a saving throw against your spell save DC.
spellcasting_basics.concentration: A caster can normally concentrate on only one concentration spell at a time and may need Constitution saves to maintain it after taking damage.

scanner_command_examples.bot_action: Find Athletics proficiency and Strength modifier, roll 1d20 + STR mod + proficiency if applicable.
Roll 1d20 and report success/failure with critical 1/20 reminders.
Find weapon attack bonus, roll attack, then offer damage roll if it hits.
Find spell attack modifier or spell DC as appropriate from the character sheet.
Roll exact dice expression as typed.

monster_reference_pattern: Use creature lore to understand motivation, habitat, tactics, and negotiation hooks without treating monsters as only stat blocks.
Keep quick indexes by challenge, environment, creature type, and role so encounters can be selected quickly during play.
Separate player-facing description from DM-only tactics, secrets, and stat-block mechanics.
adventure_module_pattern: Prepare an introduction, premise, safety expectations, starting hook, scene list, map/area keys, encounter notes, treasure/rewards, and aftermath.
Use scene goals instead of a fixed script: clue, obstacle, choice, consequence, and next lead.
For dungeon or site play, each area should answer: what is visible, what changes when characters interact, what danger or opportunity exists, and what exits lead onward.
For wilderness play, track route, weather, supplies, landmarks, hazards, safe rests, and rumors without forcing one correct path.
For sidequests and short sessions, limit the structure to one clear problem, two or three meaningful scenes, a decision point, and a consequence.
errata_and_updates_pattern: Keep a corrections log for rule clarifications, table rulings, changed homebrew, and source updates.
When a rule changes, record what changed, when it changed, and whether it affects existing characters.
encounter_design_pattern: Choose a dramatic purpose first: reveal, pressure, negotiation, travel complication, rescue, chase, survival, or boss confrontation.
Then choose creatures, terrain, stakes, starting distance, visibility, objectives besides damage, and retreat or surrender outcomes.
Balance is a guideline, not a promise; signal danger clearly and let player choices matter.

5.5e.deity_note: SRD 5.2.1 does not include the fantasy-historical pantheon tables. The sheet offers the SRD 5.1 deity list and a write-in option for campaign-approved deities.

official_character_options.write_in_policy: Race/species, gender identity, pronouns, background, subclass, and deity controls include a write-in path. Race/species write-ins are marked as requiring DM approval.

race_catalog_metadata.scope: All official Wizards-published fifth-edition playable race/species names represented in the D&D Beyond official species catalog through July 28, 2026, plus official named character-builder variants such as dragonborn lineages and Variant Human. Official subraces and lineages are also available in the option selector. Third-party marketplace species are excluded.
race_catalog_metadata.5e_behavior: Fixed legacy racial ability bonuses are applied when defined. Flexible official options automatically assign bonuses to the selected class's highest-priority abilities.
race_catalog_metadata.5_5e_behavior: Species do not supply ability-score increases; class selection generates base scores and background supplies origin increases.

formulas.skill_or_save: ability modifier + proficiency bonus when proficient, or twice proficiency with Expertise + miscellaneous bonuses
formulas.spell_save_dc: 8 + proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier + miscellaneous bonus
formulas.spell_attack_bonus: proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier + miscellaneous bonus
formulas.weapon_attack: d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient + magic/miscellaneous bonuses; compare with Armor Class
formulas.hit_points: sum of raw Hit Die gains + Constitution modifier × total character level + race/species and other bonuses
formulas.carrying_capacity: Strength score × 15 pounds, modified by size or a specific trait
formulas.push_drag_lift: Strength score × 30 pounds, modified by size or a specific trait
formulas.multiclass_spellcaster_level_5e: all full-caster levels + floor(Paladin/2) + floor(Ranger/2); qualifying one-third-caster subclasses require manual inclusion
formulas.multiclass_spellcaster_level_5_5e: all full-caster levels + ceil(Paladin/2) + ceil(Ranger/2); qualifying one-third-caster subclasses require manual inclusion

character_engine.roll_instruction_policy: The sheet displays formulas and target numbers but intentionally contains no random-number generator or dice roller.

initial_generation.assignment: Sort six generated totals from highest to lowest and assign them according to the selected class ability priority.
initial_generation.trigger: Generate when race/species and starting class are both selected or changed.

selective_rerolls.selection_rule: Only abilities whose Include in reroll checkbox is checked are rolled during that attempt.
selective_rerolls.best_result_rule: The best rolled total for every ability that participated in at least one reroll is applied automatically after the third reroll.
selective_rerolls.unchecked_rule: Unchecked ability scores remain unchanged for that attempt.

randomness.preferred_source: Web Crypto getRandomValues with rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias.
randomness.fallback: Math.random only when Web Crypto is unavailable.

notation_references.name: Dice Maiden
notation_references.use: Reference for the common 4d6-keep-highest-3 D&D stat method.

notation_references.name: Dice Witch
notation_references.use: Reference for visual tabletop-style random dice handling; no bot code is embedded.

spells.description_policy: Descriptions and casting fields are retained from the uploaded merged spell reference. Missing school/level labels are filled from its grouped indexes where possible.

abi_dalzim_s_horrid_wilting.components: V, S, M (a bit of sponge)
abi_dalzim_s_horrid_wilting.description:
You draw the moisture from every creature in a 30-foot cube centered on a point you choose within range. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. Constructs and undead aren’t affected, and plants and water elementals make this saving throw with disadvantage. A creature takes 12d8 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Nonmagical plants in the area that aren’t creatures, such as trees and shrubs, wither and die instantly.

absorb_elements.casting_time: 1 reaction, which you take when you take acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage
absorb_elements.description:
The spell captures some of the incoming energy, lessening its effect on you and storing it for your next melee attack. You have resistance to the triggering damage type until the start of your next turn. Also, the first time you hit with a melee attack on your next turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 damage of the triggering type, and the spell ends.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

acid_splash.description:
You hurl a bubble of acid. Choose one creature you can see within range, or choose two creatures you can see within range that are within 5 feet of each other. A target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 acid damage.

This spell’s damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6), and 17th level (4d6).

aganazzar_s_scorcher.components: V, S, M (a red dragon’s scale)
aganazzar_s_scorcher.description:
A line of roaring flame 30 feet long and 5 feet wide emanates from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 3d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

aid.components: V, S, M (a tiny strip of white cloth)
aid.description:
Your spell bolsters your allies with toughness and resolve. Choose up to three creatures within range. Each target’s hit point maximum and current hit points increase by 5 for the duration.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, a target’s hit points increase by an additional 5 for each slot level above 2nd.

air_bubble.description:
You create a spectral globe around the head of a willing creature you can see within range. The globe is filled with fresh air that lasts until the spell ends. If the creature has more than one head, the globe of air appears around only one of its heads (which is all the creature needs to avoid suffocation, assuming that all its heads share the same respiratory system).

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can create two additional globes of fresh air for each slot level above 2nd.

alarm.components: V, S, M (a tiny bell and a piece of fine silver wire)
alarm.description:
You set an alarm against unwanted intrusion. Choose a door, a window, or an area within range that is no larger than a 20-foot cube. Until the spell ends, an alarm alerts you whenever a Tiny or larger creature touches or enters the warded area. When you cast the spell, you can designate creatures that won’t set off the alarm. You also choose whether the alarm is mental or audible.

A mental alarm alerts you with a ping in your mind if you are within 1 mile of the warded area. This ping awakens you if you are sleeping.

An audible alarm produces the sound of a hand bell for 10 seconds within 60 feet.

alter_self.description:
You assume a different form. When you cast the spell, choose one of the following options, the effects of which last for the duration of the spell. While the spell lasts, you can end one option as an action to gain the benefits of a different one.

**Aquatic Adaptation.** You adapt your body to an aquatic environment, sprouting gills and growing webbing between your fingers. You can breathe underwater and gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. 

**Change Appearance.** You transform your appearance. You decide what you look like, including your height, weight, facial features, sound of your voice, hair length, coloration, and distinguishing characteristics, if any. You can make yourself appear as a member of another race, though none of your statistics change. You also can’t appear as a creature of a different size than you, and your basic shape stays the same; if you’re bipedal, you can’t use this spell to become quadrupedal, for instance. At any time for the duration of the spell, you can use your action to change your appearance in this way again.

**Natural Weapons.** You grow claws, fangs, spines, horns, or a different natural weapon of your choice. Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, as appropriate to the natural weapon you chose, and you are proficient with your unarmed strikes. Finally, the natural weapon is magic and you have a +1 bonus to the attack and damage rolls you make using it.

animal_friendship.components: V, S, M (a morsel of food)
animal_friendship.description:
This spell lets you convince a beast that you mean it no harm. Choose a beast that you can see within range. It must see and hear you. If the beast’s Intelligence is 4 or higher, the spell fails. Otherwise, the beast must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for the spell’s duration. If you or one of your companions harms the target, the spell ends.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can affect one additional beast for each slot level above 1st.

animal_messenger.components: V, S, M (a morsel of food)
animal_messenger.description:
By means of this spell, you use an animal to deliver a message. Choose a Tiny beast you can see within range, such as a squirrel, a blue jay, or a bat. You specify a location, which you must have visited, and a recipient who matches a general description, such as “a man or woman dressed in the uniform of the town guard” or “a red-haired dwarf wearing a pointed hat.” You also speak a message of up to twenty-five words. The target beast travels for the duration of the spell toward the specified location, covering about 50 miles per 24 hours for a flying messenger, or 25 miles for other animals.

When the messenger arrives, it delivers your message to the creature that you described, replicating the sound of your voice. The messenger speaks only to a creature matching the description you gave. If the messenger doesn’t reach its destination before the spell ends, the message is lost, and the beast makes its way back to where you cast this spell.

***At Higher Levels.*** If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the duration of the spell increases by 48 hours for each slot level above 2nd.

animal_shapes.description:
Your magic turns others into beasts. Choose any number of willing creatures that you can see within range. You transform each target into the form of a Large or smaller beast with a challenge rating of 4 or lower.  On subsequent turns, you can use your action to transform affected creatures into new forms.

The transformation lasts for the duration for each target, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies.  You can choose a different form for each target. A target’s game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the chosen beast, thought the target retains its alignment and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The target assumes the hit points of its new form, and when it reverts to its normal form, it returns to the number of hit points it had before it transformed. If it reverts as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce the creature’s normal form to 0 hit points, it isn’t knocked unconscious. The creature is limited in the actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can’t speak or cast spells.

The target’s gear melds into the new form. The target can’t activate, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment.

animate_dead.components: V, S, M (a drop of blood, a piece of flesh, and a pinch of bone dust)
animate_dead.description:
This spell creates an undead servant. Choose a pile of bones or a corpse of a Medium or Small humanoid within range. Your spell imbues the target with a foul mimicry of life, raising it as an undead creature. The target becomes a skeleton if you chose bones or a zombie if you chose a corpse (the DM has the creature’s game statistics).

On each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to mentally command any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 60 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

The creature is under your control for 24 hours, after which it stops obeying any command you’ve given it. To maintain control of the creature for another 24 hours, you must cast this spell on the creature again before the current 24-hour period ends. This use of the spell reasserts your control over up to four creatures you have animated with this spell, rather than animating a new one.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you animate or reassert control over two additional undead creatures for each slot level above 3rd. Each of the creatures must come from a different corpse or pile of bones.

animate_objects.description:
Objects come to life at your command. Choose up to ten nonmagical objects within range that are not being worn or carried. Medium targets count as two objects, Large targets count as four objects, Huge targets count as eight objects. You can’t animate any object larger than Huge. Each target animates and becomes a creature under your control until the spell ends or until reduced to 0 hit points.

As a bonus action, you can mentally command any creature you made with this spell if the creature is within 500 feet of you (if you control multiple creatures, you can command any or all of them at the same time, issuing the same command to each one). You decide what action the creature will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the creature only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.

| Size   | HP | AC | Attack                   | Str | Dex |
| ------ |:--:|:--:|:------------------------:|:---:|:---:|
| Tiny   | 20 | 18 | +8 to hit, 1d4+4 damage  |   4 |  18 |
| Small  | 25 | 16 | +6 to hit, 1d8+2 damage  |   6 |  14 |
| Medium | 40 | 13 | +5 to hit, 2d6+1 damage  |  10 |  12 |
| Large  | 50 | 10 | +6 to hit, 2d10+2 damage |  14 |  10 |
| Huge   | 80 | 10 | +8 to hit, 2d12+2 damage |  18 |   6 |

An animated object is a construct with AC, hit points, attacks, Strength, and Dexterity determined by its size. Its Constitution is 10 and its Intelligence and Wisdom are 3, and its Charisma is 1. Its speed is 30 feet; if the object lacks legs or other appendages it can use for locomotion, it instead has a flying speed of 30 feet and can hover. If the object is securely attached to a surface or a larger object, such as a chain bolted to a wall, its speed is 0. It has blindsight with a radius of 30 feet and is blind beyond that distance. When the animated object drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original object form, and any remaining damage carries over to its original object form.

If you command an object to attack, it can make a single melee attack against

antagonize.components: V, S, M (a playing card depicting a rogue)
antagonize.description:
You whisper magical words that antagonize one creature of your choice within range. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 4d4 psychic damage and must immediately use its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature of your choice that you can see. If the target can’t make this attack (for example, because there is no one within its reach or because its reaction is unavailable), the target instead has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 3rd.

antilife_shell.description:
A shimmering barrier extends out from you in a 10-foot-radius and moves with you, remaining centered on you and hedging out creatures other than undead and constructs. The barrier lasts for the duration.

The barrier prevents an affected creature from passing or reaching through. An affected creature can cast spells or make attacks with ranged or reach weapons through the barrier.

If you move so an affected creature is forced to pass through the barrier, the spell ends.

antimagic_field.components: V, S, M (a pinch of powdered iron or iron filings)
antimagic_field.description:
A 10-foot-radius invisible sphere of antimagic surrounds you. This area is divorced from the magical energy that suffuses the multiverse. Within the sphere, spells can’t be cast, summoned creatures disappear, and even magic items become mundane. Until the spell ends, the sphere moves with you, centered on you.

Spells and other magical effects, except those created by an artifact or a deity, are suppressed in the sphere and can’t protrude into it. A slot expended to cast a suppressed spell is consumed. While an effect is suppressed, it doesn’t function, but the time it spends suppressed counts against its duration.

**Targeted Effects.** Spells and other magical effects, such as *[Magic Missile](magic-missile)* and *[Charm Person](charm-person)*, that target a creature or an object in the sphere have no effect on that target.

**Areas of Magic.** The area of another spell or magical effect, such as *[Fireball](fireball)*, can’t extend into the sphere. If the sphere overlaps an area of magic, the part of the area that is covered by the sphere is suppressed. For example, the flames created by a *[Wall of Fire](wall-of-fire)* are suppressed within the sphere, creating a gap in the wall if the overlap is large enough.

**Spells.** Any active spell or other magical effect on a creature or an object in the sphere is suppressed while the creature or object is in it.

**Magic Items.** The properties and powers of magic items are suppressed in the sphere. For example, a *+1 longsword* in the sphere functions as a nonmagical longsword.

A magic weapon’s properties and powers are suppressed if it is used against a target in the sphere or wielded by an attacker in the sphere. If a magic weapon or a piece of magic ammunition fully leaves the sphere (for example, if you fire a magic arrow or throw a magic spear at a target outside the sphere), the magic of the item ceases to be suppressed as soon as it exits.

**Magical Travel.** Teleportation and planar travel fail to work in the sphere, whether the sphere is the destination or the departure point for such magical travel. A portal to another location, world, or plane of existence, as well as an opening to an extradimensional

antipathy_sympathy.components: V, S, M (either a hump of alum soaked in vinegar for the *antipathy* effect or a drop of honey for the *sympathy* effect)
antipathy_sympathy.description:
This spell attracts or repels creatures of your choice. You target something within range, either a Huge or smaller object or creature or an area that is no larger than a 200-foot cube. Then specify a kind of intelligent creature such as red dragons, goblins or vampires. You invest the target with an aura that either attracts or repels the specified creatures for the duration. Choose antipathy or sympathy as the aura’s effect.

**Antipathy.** The enchantment causes creatures of the kind you designated to feel an intense urge to leave the area and avoid the target. When such a creature can see the target or comes within 60 feet of it, the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened. The creature remains frightened while it can see the target or is within 60 feet of it. While frightened by the target, the creature must use its movement to move to the nearest safe spot from which it can’t see the target. If the creature moves more than 60 feet from the target and can’t see it, the creature is no longer frightened, but the creature becomes frightened again if it regains sight of the target or moves within 60 feet of it.

**Sympathy.** The enchantment causes the specified creatures to feel an intense urge to approach the target while within 60 feet of it or able to see it.  When such a creature can see the target or comes within 60 feet of it, the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or use its movement on each of its turns to enter the area or move within reach of the target. When the creature has done so, it can’t willingly move away from the target.

If the target damages or otherwise harms an affected creature, the affected creature can make a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect, as described below.

**Ending the Effect.** If an affected creature ends its turn while not within 60 feet of the target or able to see it, the creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, the creature is no longer affected by the target and recognizes the feeling of repugnance or attraction as magical. In addition, a creature affected by the spell is allowed another Wisdom saving throw every 24 hours while the spell persists.

A creatur

arcane_eye.components: V, S, M (a bit of bat fur)
arcane_eye.description:
You create an invisible, magical eye within range that hovers in the for the duration.

You mentally receive visual information from the eye, which has normal vision and darkvision out to 30 feet. The eye can look in every direction.

As an action, you can move the eye up to 30 feet in any direction. There is no limit to how far away from you the eye can move, but it can’t enter another plane of existence. A solid barrier blocks the eye’s movement, but the eye can pass through an opening as small as 1 inch in diameter.

arcane_gate.description:
You create linked teleportation portals that remain open for the duration. Choose two points on the ground that you can see, one point within 10 feet of you and one point within 500 feet of you. A circular portal, 10 feet in diameter, opens over each point. If the portal would open in the space occupied by a creature, the spell fails, and the casting is lost.

The portals are two-dimensional glowing rings filled with mist, hovering inches from the ground and perpendicular to it at the points you choose. A ring is visible only from one side (your choice), which is the side that functions as a portal.

Any creature or object entering the portal exits from the other portal as if the two were adjacent to each other; passing through a portal from the nonportal side has no effect. The mist that fills each portal is opaque and blocks vision through it. On your turn, you can rotate the rings as a bonus action so that the active side faces in a different direction.

arcane_lock.components: V, S, M (gold dust worth at least 25 gp, which the spell consumes)
arcane_lock.description:
You touch a closed door, window, gate, chest, or other entryway, and it becomes locked for the duration. You and the creatures you designate when you cast this spell can open the object normally. You can also set a password that, when spoken within 5 feet of the object, suppresses this spell for 1 minute. Otherwise, it is impassable until it is broken or the spell is dispelled or suppressed. Casting knock on the object suppresses arcane lock for 10 minutes.

While affected by this spell, the object is more difficult to break or force open; the DC to break it or pick any locks on it increases by 10.

armor_of_agathys.components: V, S, M (a cup of water)
armor_of_agathys.description:
A protective magical force surrounds you, manifesting as a spectral frost that covers you and your gear. You gain 5 temporary hit points for the duration. If a creature hits you with a melee attack while you have these hit points, the creature takes 5 cold damage.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, both the temporary hit points and the cold damage increase by 5 for each slot level above 1st.

arms_of_hadar.description:
You invoke the power of Hadar, the Dark Hunger. Tendrils of dark energy erupt from you and batter all creatures within 10 feet of you. Each creature in that area must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 2d6 necrotic damage and can’t take reactions until its next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, but suffers no other effect.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

ashardalon_s_stride.description:
The billowing flames of a dragon blast from your feet, granting you explosive speed. For the duration, your speed increases by 20 feet and moving doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

When you move within 5 feet of a creature or an object that isn’t being worn or carried, it takes 1d6 fire damage from your trail of heat. A creature or object can take this damage only once during a turn.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, increase your speed by 5 feet for each spell slot level above 3rd. The spell deals an additional 1d6 fire damage for each slot level above 3rd.

astral_projection.components: V, S, M (for each creature you affect with this spell you must provide one jacinth worth at least 1,000 gp and one ornately carved bar of silver worth at least 100gp, all of which the spell consumes)
astral_projection.description:
You and up to eight willing creatures within range project your astral bodies into the Astral Plane (the spell fails and the casting is wasted if you are already on that plane). The material body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation; it doesn’t need food or air and doesn’t age.

Your astral body resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics and possessions. The principal difference is the addition of a silvery cord that extends from between your shoulder blades and trails behind you, fading to invisibility after 1 foot. This cord is your tether to your material body. As long as the tether remains intact, you can find your way home. If the cord is cut---something that can happen only when an effect specifically states that it does---your soul and body are separated, killing you instantly.

Your astral form can freely travel through the Astral Plane and can pass through portals there leading to any other plane. If you enter a new plane or return to the plane you were on when casting this spell, your body and possessions are transported along the silver cord, allowing you to re-enter your body as you enter the new plane. Your astral form is a separate incarnation. Any damage or other effects that apply to it have no effect on your physical body, nor do they persist when you return to it.

The spell ends for you and your companions when you use your action to dismiss it. When the spell ends, the affected creature returns to its physical body, and it awakens.

The spell might also end early for you or one of your companions. A successful *[Dispel Magic](dispel-magic)* spell used against an astral or physical body ends the spell for that creature. If a creature’s original body or its astral form drops to 0 hit points, the spell ends for that creature. If the spell ends and the silver cord is intact, the cord pulls the creature’s astral form back to its body, ending its state of suspended animation.

If you are returned to your body prematurely, your companions remain in their astral forms and must find their own way back to their bodies, usually by dropping to 0 hit points.

augury.components: V, S, M (specially marked sticks, bones, or similar tokens worth at least 25 gp)
augury.description:
By casting gem-inlaid sticks, rolling dragon bones, laying out ornate cards, or employing some other divining tool, you receive an omen from an otherworldly entity about the results of a specific course of action that you plan to take within the next 30 minutes. The DM chooses from the following possible omens:

* *Weal*, for good results
* *Woe*, for bad results
* *Weal and woe*, for both good and bad results
* *Nothing*, for results that aren’t especially good or bad

The spell doesn’t take into account any possible circumstances that might change the outcome, such as the casting of additional spells or the loss or gain of a companion.

If you cast the spell two or more times before completing your next long rest, there is a cumulative 25 percent chance for each casting after the first that you get a random reading. The DM makes this roll in secret.

aura_of_life.description: Life-preserving energy radiates from you in an aura with a 30-foot radius. Until the spell ends, the aura moves with you, centered on you. Each nonhostile creature in the aura (including you) has resistance to necrotic damage, and its hit point maximum can’t be reduced. In addition, a nonhostile, living creature regains 1 hit point when it starts its turn in the aura with 0 hit points.

aura_of_purity.description: Purifying energy radiates from you in an aura with a 30-foot radius. Until the spell ends, the aura moves with you, centered on you. Each nonhostile creature in the aura (including you) can’t become diseased, has resistance to poison damage, and has advantage on saving throws against effects that cause any of the following conditions: blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned and stunned.

aura_of_vitality.description: Healing energy radiates from you in an aura with a 30-foot radius. Until the spell ends, the aura moves with you, centered on you. You can use a bonus action to cause one creature in the aura (including you) to regain 2d6 hit points.

awaken.components: V, S, M (an agate worth at least 1000 gp, which the spell consumes)
awaken.description:
After spending the casting time tracing magical pathways within a precious gemstone, you touch a Huge or smaller beast or plant. The target must have either no Intelligence score or an Intelligence of 3 or less. The target gains an Intelligence of 10. The target also gains the ability to speak one language you know. If the target is a plant, it gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, creepers, and so forth, and it gains senses similar to a human’s. Your DM chooses statistics appropriate for the awakened plant, such as the statistics for the awakened shrub or the awakened tree.

The awakened beast or plant is charmed by you for 30 days or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. When the charmed condition ends, the awakened creature chooses whether to remain friendly to you, based on how you treated it while it was charmed.

bane.components: V, S, M (a drop of blood)
bane.description:
Up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range must make Charisma saving throws. Whenever a target that fails this saving throw makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must roll a d4 and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll or saving throw.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

banishing_smite.description: The next time you hit a creature with a weapon attack before this spell ends, your weapon crackles with force, and the attack deals an extra 5d10 force damage to the target. Additionally, if this attack reduces the target to 50 hit points or fewer, you banish it. If the target is native to a different plane of existence than the one you’re on, the target disappears, returning to its home plane. If the target is native to the plane you’re on, the creature vanishes into a harmless demiplane. While there, the target is incapacitated. It remains there until the spell ends, at which point the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

banishment.components: V, S, M (an item distasteful to the target)
banishment.description:
You attempt to send one creature that you can see within range to another plane of existence. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished.

If the target is native to the plane of existence you’re on, you banish the target to a harmless demiplane. While there, the target is incapacitated. The target remains there until the spell ends, at which point the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

If the target is native to a different plane of existence than the one you’re on, the target is banished with a faint popping noise, returning to its home plane. If the spell ends before 1 minute has passed, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. Otherwise, the target doesn’t return.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 4th.

barkskin.components: V, S, M (a handful of oak bark)
barkskin.description: You touch a willing creature. Until the spell ends, the target’s skin has a rough, bark-like appearance, and the target’s AC can’t be less than 16, regardless of what kind of armor it is wearing.

beacon_of_hope.description: This spell bestows hope and vitality. Choose any number of creatures within range. For the duration, each target has advantage on Wisdom saving throws and death saving throws, and regains the maximum number of hit points possible from any healing.

beast_bond.components: V, S, M (a bit of fur wrapped in a cloth)
beast_bond.description: You establish a telepathic link with one beast you touch that is friendly to you or charmed by you. The spell fails if the beast’s Intelligence is 4 or higher. Until the spell ends, the link is active while you and the beast are within line of sight of each other. Through the link, the beast can understand your telepathic messages to it, and it can telepathically communicate simple emotions and concepts back to you. While the link is active, the beast gains advantage on attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you that you can see.

beast_sense.description:
You touch a willing beast. For the duration of the spell, you can use your action to see through the beast’s eyes and hear what it hears, and continue to do so until you use your action to return to your normal senses.

While perceiving through the beast’s senses, you gain the benefits of any special senses possessed by that creature, though you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.

bestow_curse.description:
You touch a creature, and that creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become cursed for the duration of the spell. When you cast this spell, choose the nature of the curse from the following options:

* Choose one ability score. While cursed, the target has disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws made with that ability score.
* While cursed, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
* While cursed, the target must make a Wisdom saving throw at the start of each of its turns. If it fails, it wastes its action that turn doing nothing.
* While the target is cursed, your attacks and spells deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage to the target.

A *[Remove Curse](remove-curse)* spell ends this effect. At the DM’s option, you may choose an alternative curse effect, but it should be no more powerful than those described above. The DM has final say on such a curse’s effect.

***At Higher Levels.*** If you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the duration is concentration, up to 10 minutes. If you use a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the duration is 8 hours. If you use a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the duration is 24 hours. If you use a 9th level spell slot, the spell lasts until it is dispelled. Using a spell slot of 5th level or higher grants a duration that doesn’t require concentration.

bigby_s_hand.components: V, S, M (an eggshell and a snakeskin glove)
bigby_s_hand.description:
You create a Large hand of shimmering, translucent force in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The hand lasts for the spell’s duration, and it moves at your command, mimicking the movements of your own hand. 

The hand is an object that has AC 20 and hit points equal to your hit point maximum. If it drops to 0 hit points, the spell ends. It has a Strength of 26 (+8) and a Dexterity of 10 (+0). The hand doesn’t fill its space. 

When you cast the spell and as a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can move the hand up to 60 feet and then cause one of the following effects with it. 

**Clenched Fist.** The hand strikes one creature or object within 5 feet of it. Make a melee spell attack for the hand using your game statistics. On a hit, the target takes 4d8 force damage.

**Forceful Hand.** The hand attempts to push a creature within 5 feet of it in a direction you choose. Make a check with the hand’s Strength contested by the Strength (Athletics) check of the target. If the target is Medium or smaller, you have advantage on the check. If you succeed, the hand pushes the target up to 5 feet plus a number of feet equal to five times your spellcasting ability modifier. The hand moves with the target to remain within 5 feet of it.

**Grasping Hand.** The hand attempts to grapple a Huge or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. You use the hand’s Strength score to resolve the grapple. If the target is Medium or smaller, you have advantage on the check. While the hand is grappling the target, you can use a bonus action to have the hand crush it. When you do so, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to 2d6 + your spellcasting ability modifier.

**Interposing Hand.** The hand interposes itself between you and a creature you choose until you give the hand a different command. The hand moves to stay between you and the target, providing you with half cover against the target. The target can’t move through the hand’s space if its Strength score is less than or equal to the hand’s Strength score. If its Strength score is higher than the hand’s Strength score, the target can move toward you through the hand’s space, but that space is difficult terrai

blade_barrier.description:
You create a vertical wall of whirling, razor-sharp blades made of magical energy. The wall appears within range and lasts for the duration. You can make a straight wall up to 100 feet long, 20 feet high, and 5 feet thick, or a ringed wall up to 60 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 5 feet thick. The wall provides three-quarters cover to creatures behind it, and its space is difficult terrain.

When a creature enters the wall’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 6d10 slashing damage. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage.

blade_of_disaster.description:
You create a blade-shaped planar rift about 3 feet long in an unoccupied space you can see within range. The blade lasts for the duration. When you cast this spell, you can make up to two melee spell attacks with the blade, each one against a creature, loose object, or structure within 5 feet of the blade. On a hit, the target takes 4d12 force damage. This attack scores a critical hit if the number on the d20 is 18 or higher. On a critical hit, the blade deals an extra 8d12 force damage (for a total of 12d12 force damage).

As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the blade up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see and then make up to two melee spell attacks with it again.

The blade can harmlessly pass through any barrier, including a wall of force.

blade_ward.description: You extend your hand and trace a sigil of warding in the air. Until the end of your next turn, you have resistance against bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage dealt by weapon attacks.

bless.components: V, S, M (a sprinkling of holy water)
bless.description:
You bless up to three creatures of your choice within range. Whenever a target makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

blight.description:
Necromantic energy washes over a creature of your choice that you can see within range, draining moisture and vitality from it. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. The target takes 8d8 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

If you target a plant creature or a magical plant, it makes the saving throw with disadvantage, and the spell deals maximum damage to it.

If you target a nonmagical plant that isn’t a creature, such as a tree or shrub, it doesn’t make a saving throw; it simply withers and dies.

***At Higher Levels.*** When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level of higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 4th.

blinding_smite.description:
The next time you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack during this spell’s duration, your weapon flares with bright light, and the attack deals an extra 3d8 radiant damage to the target. Additionally, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the spell ends.

A creature blinded by this spell makes another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, it is no longer blinded.

blindness_deafness.description:
You can blind or deafen a foe. Choose one creature that you can see within range to make a Constitution saving throw.
